2026-12-30.title: First Wednesday of Nativity
2026-12-30.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: My grace is sufficient for you
2026-12-30.alt: Mapped from the 2024–25 calendar; please verify.
2026-12-30.verse: But he said to them, “It is I; do not be afraid.”
theo: Paul, burdened by a “thorn in the flesh”, begs the Lord three times to remove it and hears: “My grace is sufficient for you, for power is made perfect in weakness.” He learns to boast of his weakness, “so that the power of Christ may dwell in me.”

The disciples row against the wind at night; Jesus comes to them walking on the sea and says, “It is I; do not be afraid.” As the year ends, many of us look back on storms and weaknesses. The Child of Bethlehem is the Lord of the storm; he comes to us in the dark and says the same words.
outline: Ask: what storm or weakness did you face this year?
God's power works through our limits.
Jesus comes to us in the dark.
Face the new year with trust.
“It is I; do not be afraid.”
live: Give God one weakness and ask for his grace.
Pray “Jesus, I trust in you” whenever anxious about the new year.
2026-12-30.prayer: Lord Jesus, you came to your disciples in the storm and said, “It is I; do not be afraid.” Let your grace be sufficient for me, and your strength work in my weakness. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana we receive the grace that is sufficient. The Lord who walked on the waters comes to us in our weakness.

quick: God's power is made perfect in weakness.
Jesus comes to us in the storm.
“It is I; do not be afraid.”
2026-12-30.question: What storm do I need to give to Jesus?

family.explain: The disciples were scared in the storm, but Jesus came to them and said: it is I; do not be afraid.
family.intention: We pray for anyone in our family who is sick or afraid.
family.ask: Ask: “What storm did Jesus help us through this year?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you come to us across the waters and say: do not be afraid. As we gather near the end of this year, give us grace that is sufficient for every need. Amen.
share: God told Paul: my grace is sufficient for you (2 Corinthians 12:9). What thorn am I carrying?
Jesus said: it is I; do not be afraid (John 6:20). What fear do I bring into the new year?
How has God's power been made perfect in my weakness this year?
pm.resp: Your grace is sufficient for us, Lord.
interc: For the Church, that she may trust the Lord in every storm.
For the chronically ill and those in pain, that they may receive sufficient grace.
For fishermen and all who work at sea, that they may be protected.
For those afraid of the coming year, that they may trust in God.
For our families, that we may thank God for the graces of this year.
pm.close: Lord God, your power is made perfect in weakness. Calm our fears, strengthen us in our thorns, and lead us into the new year with trust in your sufficient grace. Amen.

illus: A priest in Thalassery lived with chronic pain for twenty years. Asked how he kept smiling, he said: “Every morning I ask Jesus to take it away. Every morning he gives me enough grace for that day. It has never run out.”

homily: Dear friends, St Paul speaks of a thorn in his flesh, a messenger of Satan to torment him. Three times he begged the Lord to take it away. But the Lord said: my grace is sufficient for you, for power is made perfect in weakness (2 Corinthians 12:7–9).

We do not know what Paul's thorn was: an illness, a persecution, a temptation. What we know is that God did not remove it. Instead he gave grace. Paul concludes: so I will boast all the more gladly of my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may dwell in me; whenever I am weak, then I am strong (2 Corinthians 12:9–10).

At the end of the year, many of us carry thorns: illness that did not heal, a problem that was not solved, a prayer that was not answered as we wished. God's answer to Paul is also for us: my grace is sufficient for you.

In the Gospel the disciples are rowing across the lake at night in a strong wind. Then they see Jesus walking on the sea and coming near the boat, and they are terrified. But he says: it is I; do not be afraid (John 6:19–20).

Jesus comes to us across the storms, not always by stopping them, but by being with us in them. The Child of Bethlehem is the Lord of the waters. His words are the same tonight: it is I; do not be afraid.

As this year ends, let us bring our thorns and our storms to him. Let us thank him for the grace that carried us this year, and enter the new year not with fear, but with trust: his grace is sufficient. Amen.
kids: Children, when you are scared, remember Jesus says: it is I, do not be afraid. He is always near you!

intro: Theme: “It is I; do not be afraid.”
Grace in weakness; Jesus walking on the sea.

sub: God parted the sea for Israel.
q: Then Moses stretched out his hand over the sea. The LORD drove the sea back by a strong east wind all night, and turned the sea into dry land; and the waters were divided.
When they had rowed about three or four miles, they saw Jesus walking on the sea and coming near the boat, and they were terrified.
points.apply: Name one storm and give it to Jesus.

q: He made the storm be still, and the waves of the sea were hushed.
But he said to them, “It is I; do not be afraid.”
points.apply: Pray “Jesus, I trust in you” when anxious.

sub: Weakness becomes the place of Christ's power.
q: But those who wait for the LORD shall renew their strength.
But he said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for power is made perfect in weakness.”

concl: The Lord of the storm is with us.
His grace is enough for the new year.
2026-12-30.resolve: Enter the new year with an act of trust.
